title: The Lion Becomes the King of Beasts, part 3
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: The great spider was lying asleep when the Lion found him, and it looked so ugly that its foe turned up his nose in disgust. Its legs were quite as long as the tiger had said, and its body covered with coarse black hair. It had a great mouth, with a row of sharp teeth a foot long; but its head was joined to the pudgy body by a neck as slender as a wasp’s waist. This gave the Lion a hint of the best way to attack the creature, and as he knew it was easier to fight it asleep than awake, he gave a great spring and landed directly upon the monster’s back. Then, with one blow of his heavy paw, all armed with sharp claws, he knocked the spider’s head from its body. Jumping down, he watched it until the long legs stopped wiggling, when he knew it was quite dead.
The Lion went back to the opening where the beasts of the forest were waiting for him and said proudly:
“You need fear your enemy no longer.”
Then the beasts bowed down to the Lion as their King, and he promised to come back and rule over them as soon as Dorothy was safely on her way to Kansas.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the spider doing when the Lion found it?
options: Lying asleep
Eating one of the beasts
Climbing among the oak trees
Waiting for him, wide awake

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what covered the spider's body?
options: Coarse black hair
Smooth green scales
A shell like a beetle's
Fine white fur

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how long were the spider's teeth?
options: A foot long
An inch long
As long as an arm
It had no teeth at all

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what was the spider's neck like?
options: As slender as a wasp's waist
As thick as a tree trunk
Covered in the same black hair
Too short to be seen at all

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Lion kill the monster?
options: One blow of his paw knocked its head off
He bit through its slender neck
He rolled it into the marsh to drown
He drove it off the edge of a cliff

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what gave the Lion his plan of attack?
options: The slenderness of the monster's neck
The length of its eight long legs
The fact that it was covered in hair
The tiger's description of its mouth

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Lion attack while it slept?
options: He knew it was easier to fight asleep than awake
He was too frightened to face it waking
The beasts had told him to do it that way
He wanted to be back before nightfall

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the Lion make sure it was dead?
options: He watched until the long legs stopped wiggling
He struck it a second time with his paw
He called the tigers over to look at it
He dragged the body back to the clearing

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does pudgy describe?
options: The short thick body of the spider
The hair growing on its legs
The slenderness of its neck
The length of its sharp teeth

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A single well-judged blow wins the Lion a kingdom
A long battle in which the Lion is badly wounded
The Lion finds the monster too large to fight
The beasts refuse to accept the Lion as their king

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Lion reach the monster's back?
options: With a great spring
By climbing an oak tree
By crawling under its legs
By waiting for it to lie down

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Lion tell the beasts on his return?
options: That they need fear their enemy no longer
That the monster was too strong
That he would need their help to finish it
That he was leaving the forest

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when did the Lion promise to return and rule?
options: As soon as Dorothy was safely on her way to Kansas
Within a year and a day of the fight
Once Glinda had given her permission
As soon as the Scarecrow released him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what was the Lion's first reaction to the spider?
options: He turned up his nose in disgust at how ugly it was
He was too frightened to come any nearer
He was surprised at how small it really was
He admired the creature's great strength

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how does the Lion speak when he returns?
options: Proudly
Modestly
Fearfully
Angrily

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does foe mean?
options: Enemy
Hunter
Visitor
Ruler

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: The Lion earns by one stroke the title he was always given
The Lion is defeated and driven out of the forest
The beasts kill the monster while the Lion watches
The Lion decides to stay and rule at once
